title.narrative: Second Upper Secondary Education Sector Development Program

description.narrative: The proposed Second Upper Secondary Education Sector Development Program (USESDP 2) is part of the phased support of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to develop high-quality human resources by improving the effectiveness of upper secondary education (USE). It builds on and complements ADB's ongoing Upper Secondary Education Sector Development Program (USESDP 1). The program will (i) improve teacher quality and boost the quality and labor market relevance of USE; and (ii) strengthen institutional capacity for USE planning, management, and delivery. While the policy reforms will apply nationwide, the project activities will cover only selected areas.

description.narrative: Effectiveness of the USE system improved

GER for USE increased to 31.8% (male: 26.8%; female: 34.6%; rural 29.2%) Progress/Status: Achieved
• Overall: Increased from 25.1% at the baseline to 40.4% in 2024-2025 (increased by 15.3 percentage points compared to the baseline of 2016-2017) being 8.6 percentage points higher than the DMF target of 31.8%. • Male: Increased from 23.6% at the baseline to 34.8% in 2024-2025 (increased by 11.2 percentage point compared to the baseline of 2016-2017) being 8.0 percentage points higher than the DMF target of 26.8% • Female: Increased from 26.7% at the baseline to 46.3% in 2024-2025 (increased by 19.6 percentage point as compared to the baseline of 2016-2017) being 11.7 percentage points higher than the DMF target of 34.6% • Rural: Increased from 21.4% at the baseline to 36.9% in 2024-2025 (increased by 15.5 percentage point compared to the baseline of 2016-2017) being 7.0 percentage point higher than the DMF target of 29.2%. Source: EMIS 2024-25 Data Source: MoEYS EMIS (annually) Baseline value: 23.6%;26.7%;21.4%

Grade 10 to 11 promotion rate increased to at least 90.1% (male: 89.2%; female: 90.7%; rural: 87.2%); Progress/Status: Achieved The promotion rate for 2024-2025 will be reported in EMIS 2025-2026. More efforts are needed in order to achieve the target by 2025, especially for male and overall: Overall: 87.1% (2024) vs.90.1% (2025) Male: 84.4% (2024) vs.89.2% (2025) Female: 89.4% (2024) vs.90.7% (2025) Rural: 85.1% (2024) vs.87.2% (2025) Department of Policy (DoPo) conduced the research of reasons affected the unmet outcome indicators. The report was sent to ADB on 5 June 2025 and presented and discussed on 10 June during the ADB mission. Data Source: MoEYS EMIS (annually) Baseline value: 84.8%;86.1%;83.3%

Grade 11 to 12 promotion rate increased to 97.0% (male: 96.5%; female: 97.4%; rural: 93.2%) Progress/Status: The promotion rate for 2024-2025 will be reported in EMIS 2025-2026.
More efforts are needed in order to achieve the target by 2025, especially for male and overall: Overall: 91.8% (2024) vs.97.0% (2025) Male: 89.7% (2024) vs.96.5% (2025) Female: 93.5% (2024) vs.97.4% (2025) Rural: 90.2% (2024) vs.93.2% (2025) DoPo conduced the research of reasons affected the unmet outcome indicators. The report was sent to ADB on 5 June 2025 and presented and discussed on 10 June during the ADB mission. Data Source: MoEYS EMIS (annually) Baseline value: 91.9%; 94.2%;89.3%

USE dropout rate decreased to 15.0% (male: 16.4%; female: 13.1%; rural: 15.8%) Progress/Status: • Overall: Decreased from 18.3% at the baseline to 13.7% in 2023-2024 (decreased by 4.6 percentage point as compared to the baseline of 2016-2017), and is 1.3 percentage points lower than the DMF target (15.0%) • Male: Decreased from 19.7% at the baseline to 16.2% in 2023-2024 (decreased by 3.5 percentage point compared to the baseline of 2016-2017), and it is 0.2 percentage point lower than the DMF target (16.4%) • Female: Decreased from 17.0% at the baseline to 11.6% in 2023-2024 (Decreased by 5.4 percentage point compared to the baseline of 2016-2017), and it is 1.5 percentage points lower than the DMF target (13.1%) • Rural: Decreased from 19.7% at the baseline to 14.1% in 2023-2024 (decreased by 5.6 percentage points compared to the baseline of 2016-2017), and it is 1.7 percentage points lower than the DMF target (15.8%) Source: EMIS 2024-2025 Data Source: MoEYS EMIS (annually) Baseline value: 19.7%;17%;19.7
